chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: The she-brick that spits on you
summary: Danny explains a loose paving brick that squirts water, and his grandfather's skill in avoiding it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You'd see little kids, you know, who were just fascinated by what they were playing in the street. And you would have to watch for a (?) stone or a she-brick. Now, what you call a she-brick is when it rains. See, in a loose brick, the water is under this brick...
And you call that a she-brick.
Yeah. See, it will piss on you!

See, if you walk under... [AWAY FROM MICROPHONE, NOT AUDIBLE] ...all over my pants(?), we have a she-brick. Or heave(?) a stone, see. See, my grandfather was a master at watching stones, Old Man Barbarin. See, he could dig back around the stone(?)... [BOTH LAUGH]
